title: 五步救活全场最差的马
title_en: Five Moves to Resurrect Your Worst Piece
summary: 没有直接战术时，不要乱找将军；找到最差的棋子，为它规划一条通往前哨的路线。
summary_en: With no direct tactics, don't hunt for checks; find your worst piece and plan a route to an outpost.
topic: 改善最差棋子与建立前哨
topic_en: Improving the worst piece and building an outpost
introduction: 局面平静时，很多棋手会随手推一个边兵，因为至少看起来做了什么。更可靠的问题是：我哪枚棋子最差，它怎样才能真正参加战斗？
白方 b1 的马仍在原位，其他棋子已经开始工作。你的五步计划是为它找到路线，让它最终站到 f5，并用中心兵巩固成果。
introduction_en: When the position is calm, many players push a random flank pawn just to feel they did something. A more reliable question: which of my pieces is the worst, and how can it actually join the fight?
White's knight on b1 is still on its starting square while the rest of the army works. Your five-move plan is to find its route, land it on f5, and consolidate with a center pawn.

culture.title: 最差棋子原则
culture.content: 卡帕布兰卡等位置型大师常把复杂计划压缩成一个简单动作：改善全场最差的棋子。这个原则不会直接给出唯一答案，却能在没有战术时稳定地产生候选着。

culture_en.title: The worst-piece principle
culture_en.content: Positional masters from Capablanca onward often compress a complex plan into one simple action: improve the worst piece on the board. The principle rarely names a unique move, but it reliably produces candidate moves when there is no tactic.

challenge.title: 为 b1 的马规划五步路线
challenge.instruction: 沿 d2、f1、g3、f5 改善白马，最后用 d4 加固中心。每一步都要服务于同一计划。
challenge.goal: 白方走五步，把最差的马送到前哨并巩固中心。

steps.note: 第一步正确：Nbd2 让马离开后排，并保留去 f1、f5 的路线。
第二步正确：Nf1 看似后退，实际是在转向 g3。位置棋允许为了更好路线暂时远离中心。
第三步正确：Ng3 开始瞄准 f5 和 h5，马已经从旁观者变成潜在进攻子。
第四步正确：Nf5 占据前哨，直接靠近黑王，并让黑方很难用兵驱赶。
第五步正确：d4 加固中心并限制黑方 e5 兵，让 f5 的马拥有更稳定的支点。

challenge.success: 五步完成。白马从 b1 绕到 f5，最后用 d4 稳住中心。没有任何一步直接赢子，但全队协调与进攻潜力明显提高。
challenge.defaultAnswer: 这套计划用路线而不是单步评价棋子：Nd2 和 Nf1 看起来慢，只有看到 Ng3-f5 的终点才知道它们的意义。d4 则让前哨更稳定。

errors.b1c3: Nc3 是自然发展，但 c3 已被白兵占据，而且本局马的理想路线是 d2-f1-g3-f5。
errors.h2h3: h3 是有用的等待着，却没有改善全场最差的 b1 马。没有战术时，优先解决最差棋子。

challenge.genericError: 这步可能改善了局面的一部分，但请回到本题目标：为 b1 的马规划一条完整路线。

quick.为什么马要后退: Nf1 是路线中的转弯，不是退缩。马从 f1 能去 g3，再进入 f5 前哨。
quick.什么是前哨: 前哨是深入对方阵地、又难被敌兵驱赶的稳定格。f5 的马靠近黑王，并限制多枚黑子。
quick.为什么最后走d4: 马到 f5 后，d4 加强中心控制并限制 e5，让黑方更难通过中心反击赶走白马。

challenge_en.title: Plan a five-move route for the b1 knight
challenge_en.instruction: Improve the white knight along d2, f1, g3, f5, then reinforce the center with d4. Every move serves the same plan.
challenge_en.goal: White moves five times, delivering the worst knight to an outpost and consolidating the center.

steps.note: First move correct: Nbd2 lifts the knight off the back rank while keeping the route to f1 and f5 open.
Second move correct: Nf1 looks like a retreat but is actually a turn toward g3. Positional play may move away from the center temporarily for a better route.
Third move correct: Ng3 begins aiming at f5 and h5; the knight is turning from an onlooker into a potential attacker.
Fourth move correct: Nf5 occupies the outpost, directly approaching the black king and becoming hard to drive away with pawns.
Fifth move correct: d4 reinforces the center and restricts Black's e5 pawn, giving the f5 knight a steadier base.

challenge_en.success: Five moves complete. The white knight traveled from b1 to f5, then d4 stabilized the center. No single move wins material, yet the whole army's coordination and attacking potential clearly improved.
challenge_en.defaultAnswer: This plan judges pieces by routes rather than single moves: Nd2 and Nf1 look slow, and only by seeing the Ng3-f5 destination do they make sense. d4 then makes the outpost more stable.

errors.b1c3: Nc3 is natural development, but c3 is already occupied by a white pawn, and this knight's ideal route is d2-f1-g3-f5.
errors.h2h3: h3 is a useful waiting move, but it does not improve the worst piece on the board, the b1 knight. With no tactics, fix the worst piece first.

challenge_en.genericError: This move may improve part of the position, but return to the lesson's goal: plan a complete route for the b1 knight.

quick.为什么马要后退: Nf1 is a turn in the route, not a retreat. From f1 the knight reaches g3, then enters the f5 outpost.
quick.什么是前哨: An outpost is a stable square deep in enemy territory that is hard for enemy pawns to chase away. The knight on f5 sits near the black king and restricts several black pieces.
quick.为什么最后走d4: Once the knight is on f5, d4 strengthens central control and restricts e5, making it harder for Black to counter in the center and drive the knight back.

suggestions.label: Why does the knight step backward first?

review.title: 先看终点，再评价路线
steps: Nbd2 让马离开初始格，并建立转移路线。
Nf1-g3 是典型的重组：单步看似慢，组合起来目标明确。
Nf5 抵达难被兵驱赶的前哨。
d4 用中心控制巩固马的成果，计划从棋子改善扩展到全局协调。
review.principle: 没有直接战术时，找到最差的棋子，为它设计两到三站的路线，而不是随手走一个看起来有用的兵步。

review_en.title: Judge the route by its destination
steps: Nbd2 takes the knight off its starting square and establishes a transfer route.
Nf1-g3 is a classic regrouping: each step looks slow, but together they have a clear aim.
Nf5 reaches an outpost that pawns can hardly drive away.
d4 consolidates the knight's work with central control, growing from piece improvement to whole-board coordination.
review_en.principle: With no direct tactics, find your worst piece and design a two- or three-stop route for it, instead of playing a convenient-looking pawn move.
